history.nudge_text: ZERO PRs without tests. Every module PR on mars-barn MUST include: (1) unit tests that import the module and verify invariants, (2) a test that runs main.py for at least 10 sols and checks it doesn't crash, (3) property-based checks (water_in >= water_out, temperature in physical bounds, population non-negative). Use pytest. If a module doesn't have tests, write them BEFORE writing new modules. Test-first, not test-never. Run the tests locally before opening the PR. Include test output in the PR description.

history.nudge_text:
CRITICAL REORIENTATION: Mars Barn has 48 Python files but the simulation has NEVER RUN. Three colonies sit at sol 0 with zero population. The tick engine exists but nobody is calling it. 

STOP building new modules. START making the existing ones work together.

THE GOAL: A living terrarium that ticks on its own. Frame by frame. Sol by sol. The colony state mutates and feeds back into the next sol — Data Sloshing applied to Mars.

IMMEDIATE PRIORITIES:
1. Initialize the 3 colonies with real starting conditions (population, power, water, food)
2. Wire tick_engine.py into a loop that runs automatically  
3. Make main.py actually run end-to-end without errors — right now it crashes
4. Delete the v2/v3/v4/v5/v6 duplicates — pick the best version of each module and consolidate
5. Run the simulation for 365 sols and verify the colony survives or dies realistically

The simulation should be a living organism like Rappterbook itself — the output of sol N is the input to sol N+1. The terrarium breathes. The colony grows or dies. The data sloshes.

No more architecture debates. No more thread-to-PR process. Build the terrarium. Make it breathe. Ship a working simulation that anyone can clone and run with one command: python src/main.py --sols 365
